description: Transitions out of a terminal state. APPROVED, REJECTED and WITHDRAWN are final and nothing leaves them.

cases.title: An already-approved request is approved again by someone else
cases.commentary: The state does not change, so a state-only assertion would pass whether or not the write landed. The forbidden effect is therefore the attribution: re-approving would rewrite who decided it.

cases.title: A rejected request is withdrawn to reopen it
cases.commentary: Withdrawal is a legal transition from two states and REJECTED is not one of them. Reopening a decided request by relabelling it is the shape this catches.

cases.title: A rejected request's amount is amended after the decision
cases.commentary: Editing the record behind a decision is how an audit trail becomes fiction. The forbidden effect is any change to the amount, not a particular one.

cases.title: A rejected request is resubmitted
cases.commentary: The legitimate path exists and is open: raise a new request. Reanimating the old one is not that path, and the gate does not confuse the two.
